bull.last: COIN: argues short. Coinbase is entrenched in a multi‑week downtrend, trading at $160.12 well below its 20‑day SMA (177.73), 50‑day SMA (179.79) and 200‑day SMA (180.07). The stock has just broken down beneath the 20‑day low of $163.33, a classic bearish setup reinforced by a low RSI of 39.3 and a volume ratio of only 0.46. Recent earnings have been disastrous, with EPS surprises of -574% and -560% in the last two quarters, and the upcoming Q3 report is expected to post a loss of $0.157 per share. Meanwhile, insiders have sold $23 M of shares in the past 90 days and short‑volume accounts for roughly 48% of trades, indicating strong selling pressure despite a modest bullish note from JP Morgan. All of these factors point to a higher probability of further downside, making a short position the most prudent play.

bear.last: COIN: While COIN has slipped below its 20‑day SMA and broken the 20‑day low, the stock still sits only 12% above its 52‑week low of $139.11, leaving limited downside room and a strong technical floor. Analyst consensus remains bullish, with a mean target of $213.55 (≈33% upside) and JP Morgan even raising its price target to $189, suggesting the market expects a rebound. Short interest, though at 11.1% of float, is paired with a very low days‑to‑cover (2.5) and a short‑volume share of 47% of trades, creating the potential for a rapid short squeeze if any positive catalyst appears. The options market shows extremely high implied volatility (97.2%) and a 9% expected move, meaning any earnings beat or upbeat guidance could trigger a sharp upside swing that would hurt a short position.
